gaps.sentence: He felt he was ___ for the work he did, so he asked for a raise (PAY).
gaps.hint: paid too little — he wants a raise (under-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix under- means too little: underpaid means paid less than deserved, which explains asking for a raise.

gaps.sentence: He is very ___ about local history (KNOW).
gaps.explanation: 'Knowledgeable about something' means knowing a lot about it; it is the adjective form of 'knowledge'.

gaps.sentence: The government wants to ___ the tax system (SIMPLE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: simplify means to make simple. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: His sudden ___ came as a shock to everyone (DEPART).
gaps.hint: noun needed as subject (-ure); beware the word meaning 'part of an organisation'
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'depart' is departure (-ure); a department is a section of an organisation.

gaps.sentence: She showed great ___ (PATIENT) with the children.
gaps.hint: noun needed; beware the similar word meaning 'people in hospital'
gaps.explanation: 'Patience' is the noun (show patience); 'patients' are people receiving medical care.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (ARRIVE) of the train was announced.
gaps.explanation: The subject must be a noun: arrival (-al noun of 'arrive').

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.sentence: She was fired for ___ behaviour at work (PROFESSIONAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'behaviour'
gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unprofessional behaviour is behaviour below professional standards.
